text.tspan: Income inequality vs. GDP per capita1985 to 2025
The Gini coefficient measures inequality on a scale from 0 to 1. Higher values indicate higher inequality. GDP
per capita is adjusted for inflation and differences in living costs between countries.
GDP per capita (international-$ in 2021 prices; plotted on a logarithmic axis)
Data source: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform (2026); Eurostat, OECD, IMF, and World Bank (2026)
Note: GDP per capita is expressed in international-$ at 2021 prices. Depending on the country and year, inequality data relates to income
(measured after taxes and benefits) or to consumption, per capita.
